title: Why Won't Your TOES Move One at a Time? 🦶
description:
Lift your big toe. Easy. Now lift just the next one... and the whole gang comes along. Your big toe has its own lifting muscle, but the other four mostly share ONE long muscle that splits into four strings (tendons), so when it pulls, they all come. Curling works the same way underneath: one long curling muscle, four strings. Your brain doesn't help much either: in a 2019 brain-scan study (Cell Reports), nine typical people showed no neat map of separate toes, while two artists born without arms, who paint with their feet, had a separate spot for every toe. Practice may be part of it, so big toe first. (If your foot cramps, stop.) Did the whole gang come? Yes or no?
